title: Tensor-of-counits cup coherence under group and scalar restriction
statement:
Fix the small coherent profinite site and a coefficient universe containing its objects, morphisms and all section sets below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $\mathcal M_R$ be its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $J,H$ be topological groups. Write $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ and $\mathcal A_R(J)$ for internal $R$-modules with a natural $\underline J$-action by linear automorphisms [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the normalized functors of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]: $T_J$ is trivial inflation, $\Gamma_{R,J}$ is the invariant subsheaf with its specified inclusion, $L_J=D(T_J)$, $F_J=R\Gamma_{R,J}$ with its canonical computation unit $\alpha_J$, and $L_J\dashv F_J$ is the canonical derived adjunction, with unit $\eta_J$ and counit $\varepsilon_J$. For a continuous homomorphism $u:H\to J$ put $U=D(u^*)$.

Equip the ordinary derived categories of base and action modules with internal derived tensor, using K-flat representatives and the signed total-complex comparisons. Use the diagonal action tensor of [def-sfb-condensed-action-tensor], the fixed cup pairings of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup], and the scalar tensor comparisons of [def-sfb-condensed-scalar-tensor]. Then $L_J$ is strong symmetric monoidal with the specified trivial-action tensorator. Its right adjoint has the lax pairing $\mu_J$ and unit $e_J$ uniquely specified by the following adjunction transposes:
$$\mu_{J,A,B}:F_JA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F_JB\to F_J(A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B),\qquad
\mu_{J,A,B}^{\flat}=(\varepsilon_{J,A}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\varepsilon_{J,B})\circ t_{J,F_JA,F_JB},$$
where $t_J:L_J(X\otimes^{\mathbf L}Y)\simeq L_JX\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_JY$ is the specified tensorator; the transpose of $e_J:R[0]\to F_JR[0]$ is the unit comparison $L_JR[0]\simeq R[0]$. These maps satisfy lax associativity and both unit equations, and the actual adjunction unit and counit are monoidal. In particular they give the associative unital cup algebra on $C_R(J)=F_J(R[0])$.

For all action-derived objects $A,B$, the normalized group mate $b_u$ satisfies
$$b_{u,A\otimes B}\circ\mu_{J,A,B}=F_H(t_U^{-1})\circ\mu_{H,UA,UB}\circ(b_{u,A}\otimes b_{u,B}),$$
where $t_U:U(A\otimes B)\simeq UA\otimes UB$ is the restriction tensorator; it also preserves the above unit under the regular-unit identification. For every condensed ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$, the scalar comparison $d_J:F_J^Rs_J\simeq s_0F_J^{R'}$ is monoidal for the composite lax structures. Consequently the coefficient arrow $c_J(\varphi):C_R(J)\to s_0C_{R'}(J)$ is an algebra map, with the lax scalar tensor product and unit on its target. Both group and coefficient arrows preserve all ordered finite cup products, including the empty product, with exactly the specified tensor and shift comparisons and without permuting factors. No flatness of the coefficient map is assumed.

proof.text:
Present the base condensed module category and each action category as module sheaves on the small base and action sites. The given $u:H\to J$ is a continuous group homomorphism, so postcomposition on continuous sections defines the group-sheaf map used for action restriction. The action-topos statement applies to the group sheaf $\underline J$ (and to $\underline H$), supplied by the action infrastructure. It identifies $T_J$ and $u^*$ with the exact module pullbacks $p_J^*$ and $q_u^*$, with the prescribed pure-tensor and regular-unit comparisons. Their canonical derived pullbacks therefore identify with $L_J$ and $U$. The ringed derived comparison theorem gives strong symmetric monoidal structures with exactly the K-flat tensorators and signed symmetries in the question. The ordinary right-adjoint Hom formula is the invariant-inclusion formula of the action infrastructure, so its canonical derived adjunction is the specified one, with the same computation units and counits. In particular, for $z:L_H\simeq UL_J$ induced by $p_Jq_u\cong p_H$, its tensor equation is
$$(z_X\otimes z_Y)t_{H;X,Y}=t_{U;L_JX,L_JY}\,U(t_{J;X,Y})\,z_{X\otimes Y}.$$
Here and below composition is read right to left; tensors are derived unless specified otherwise.

proof.text: Apply the monoidal-adjunction mate bijection to $L_J\dashv F_J$ and its inverse strong tensor structure. It gives a lax structure on $F_J$. Its tensor map is precisely the transpose of $(\varepsilon_{J,A}\otimes\varepsilon_{J,B})t_{J;F_JA,F_JB}$ and its unit is the transpose of the regular-unit comparison. The bijection includes the associativity and both unit axioms, and injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives uniqueness of these maps. The unit/counit theorem then makes the actual $\eta_J,\varepsilon_J$ monoidal, rather than replacing the adjunction by an unspecified isomorphic one. Repeat for $H$ and for $R'$; the cup definition uses these same mate maps.

proof.text:
Use the normalized restriction theorem, so $b_{u,A}$ has $L_H\dashv F_H$ transpose $U(\varepsilon_{J,A})z_{F_JA}$. Set $X=F_JA$, $Y=F_JB$. The transpose of $b_{u,A\otimes B}\mu_{J;A,B}$ is
$$U((\varepsilon_{J,A}\otimes\varepsilon_{J,B})t_{J;X,Y})z_{X\otimes Y}.$$
Naturality of $\varepsilon_H$ and the defining transpose of $\mu_H$ make the transpose of $F_H(t_U^{-1})\mu_{H;UA,UB}(b_{u,A}\otimes b_{u,B})$ equal to
$$t_{U;A,B}^{-1}(U\varepsilon_{J,A}\otimes U\varepsilon_{J,B})(z_X\otimes z_Y)t_{H;X,Y}.$$
Substitute the tensor equation for $z$ from step 1. Naturality of $t_U$ cancels $t_{U;A,B}^{-1}$ against $t_{U;L_JX,L_JY}$ around the tensor of counits, giving exactly the first displayed transpose. Injectivity of the Hom bijection proves the asserted group tensor equation.

proof.text: For the group unit, transpose $b_{u,\mathbf1}e_J$ under $L_H\dashv F_H$. The restriction transpose and naturality of $z$ give $U(\varepsilon_{J,\mathbf1}L_J(e_J))z_{\mathbf1}$. By the defining unit transpose this is $U(e^L_J)z_{\mathbf1}$, where $e^L_J:L_J\mathbf1\simeq\mathbf1$ is the inverse strong unit map. The unit equation for the monoidal comparison $z$, followed by the regular-unit identification of $U$, identifies this with $e^L_H$. That is the transpose of $e_H$. Thus the same group map preserves the actual unit.

proof.text: For the ring map $\varphi$, on the base site and on each action site regard scalar extension as the module pullback along the identity underlying geometric morphism. Its derived functor $E_i\dashv s_i$ is strong symmetric monoidal by the ringed comparison theorem. Apply the scalar-lax normalization lemma on each of these small sites, and use their module identifications from step 1. It identifies the right-adjoint mate structure of $s_i$ with the fixed balanced scalar tensor of the question: write its tensor and unit as $\sigma_i,\sigma_{i,0}$ for $i=0,J$. Its representative equation includes the noninvertible localization map on scalar-restricted complexes. Thus no $R$-flatness or $R$-K-flatness of an $R'$-resolution is used. The unit/counit theorem makes the scalar-adjunction units and counits monoidal for these fixed structures.

proof.text:
The ringed square supplied by the action-topos theorem has identity comparison on underlying sheaves. Its derived pullback comparison
$$\theta:E_JL_J^R\xrightarrow{\sim}L_J^{R'}E_0$$
is monoidal, including its unit: it is the composite of the normalized pullback composition comparisons and the ring-compatible geometric isomorphism of the ringed theorem. With the contravariant convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], use the inverse of this left comparison for the arrow from $P=F_J^Rs_J$ to $Q=s_0F_J^{R'}$. The scalar interchange theorem identifies that right-adjoint conjugate with the computation-unit-normalized $d_J:F_J^Rs_J\simeq s_0F_J^{R'}$ in the question. We use that identification as a statement, not an unproved inference that arbitrary right-derived functors commute with scalar restriction.

proof.text:
Write $A=E_JL_J^R$, $B=L_J^{R'}E_0$, $P=F_J^Rs_J$, $Q=s_0F_J^{R'}$. Give $P,Q$ their composite lax structures, for example $\mu^P=F_J^R(\sigma_J)\mu_J^R$. By the composite-adjunction formulas, the counit for $A\dashv P$ is $\epsilon^{E_J}\,E_J(\varepsilon^R_Js_J)$, and its unit is $F_J^R(\eta^{E_J}L_J^R)\eta^R_J$; the formulas for $B\dashv Q$ are the corresponding ones with $L_J^{R'},E_0$. These units and counits are monoidal: each is a composite of whiskered monoidal units or counits from steps 2 and 5. To check the operation used here, if $a:V\Rightarrow W$ and $b:W\Rightarrow Z$ obey the tensor equations, then
$$(ba)_{X\otimes Y}\mu^V=b_{X\otimes Y}\mu^W(a_X\otimes a_Y)=\mu^Z(b_Xa_X\otimes b_Ya_Y).$$
Their unit equations compose in the same order. Whiskering obeys the same equation by naturality of the outer lax tensor map and the formula for a composite lax tensor. This checks these particular composite units and counits directly.

proof.text:
The conjugate from step 6 has the following actual formula, using the composite adjunctions of step 7:
$$d_{J,N'}=Q(\epsilon^A_{N'})\,Q(\theta^{-1}_{PN'})\,\eta^B_{PN'}.$$
The types are $PN'\to QBPN'\to QAPN'\to QN'$. The first and last natural transformations are whiskered monoidal unit/counit transformations by step 7. The middle one is monoidal because $\theta$ is monoidal, its inverse satisfies the tensor equation after cancellation of its invertible components, and $Q$ is lax. More explicitly, if $a$ is monoidal and $V$ lax, naturality gives
$$V(a_{X\otimes Y})V(\mu^{\rm source}_{X,Y})\mu^V=V(\mu^{\rm target}_{X,Y})\mu^V(Va_X\otimes Va_Y).$$
The analogous unit equality follows by applying $V$ to the unit equation for $a$. Compose the three tensor equations by the expansion in step 7, and likewise their unit equations. This proves monoidality of the normalized $d_J$ for the composite lax structures $P,Q$.

proof.text: Let $I_R$ be the action tensor unit, identified with the actual trivial regular complex $R[0]$. Its canonical multiplication is its unitor. Under a lax monoidal functor $F_J$, its multiplication becomes $m_J=F_J(m_{I_R})\mu_{J;I_R,I_R}$ and its unit becomes $e_J$ followed by the regular identification. The lax associativity equation followed by $F_J$ of the unit-object associativity equation gives the associative law for $m_J$; the two lax unit equations give its left and right unit laws. This is exactly the cup algebra fixed in the cup definition. The group tensor and unit equations of steps 3 and 4, evaluated at $I_R$ and followed by its multiplication, show that the specified group arrow is an algebra morphism, since $U$ sends the regular-unit multiplication to the same multiplication.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice input; agent-written cup and restriction mate calculation, using the cited generic statements.

proof.text: Put $v:I_R\to s_JI_{R'}$ equal to the specified regular coefficient map. It is the scalar lax unit $\sigma_{J,0}$ from step 5. The two lax unit equations identify the multiplication on the lax image of a unit object, so $v$ is a monoid map to that lax image: $v m_{I_R}=s_J(m_{I_{R'}})\sigma_J(v\otimes v)$ and it preserves the unit. These are also the balanced formulas $\varphi(ab)=\varphi(a)\varphi(b)$ and $\varphi(1)=1$, with the scalar tensor preceding multiplication. Apply $F_J^R$ and its lax structure; naturality of $\mu_J^R$ makes $F_J^R(v)$ a monoid map. Step 8 makes $d_J(I_{R'})$ a monoid map to the lax scalar image of $C_{R'}(J)$. Their composite is precisely $c_J(\varphi)=d_J(I_{R'})F_J^R(v)$ by the scalar-tensor definition. Thus the actual coefficient arrow preserves both product and unit, for arbitrary $\varphi$.

proof.text:
Use the right-associated powers and products of the cup definition. For an algebra arrow $h:X\to VY$, define $h_0:\mathbf1\to V\mathbf1$ to be the lax unit of $V$ and $h_{n+1}=\mu^V_{Y,Y^{\otimes n}}(h\otimes h_n)$. Binary multiplicativity and naturality give the induction
$$h m_{X,n+1}=h m_X(1\otimes m_{X,n})=V(m_Y)\mu^V(h\otimes V(m_{Y,n})h_n)=V(m_{Y,n+1})h_{n+1}.$$
The base $n=0$ is unit preservation. For the group arrow take $V$ to be the identity base functor; for the coefficient arrow take $V=s_0$ with its fixed scalar lax structure. This proves preservation of every ordered finite product, including the empty product, using the specified parenthesization and no braiding.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice input; agent-written cup and restriction mate calculation, using the cited generic statements.

proof.text: Finally precompose the finite-product equalities with tensors of homogeneous class arrows from shifted regular units. The restriction normalization and scalar-interchange statements say $b_u,d_J$ commute with the fixed shifts; the regular coefficient arrow is the actual degree-zero map. The scalar normalization lemma fixes the same signed shift comparisons for $\sigma_i$. The derived tensor/shift theorem gives naturality of the specified integer shift extraction isomorphisms for every derived arrow. Concretely on a $(p,q)$ total summand, extracting a shift $a$ from the second factor multiplies by $(-1)^{ap}$; all the tensor and scalar maps used above preserve the two summand degrees, so this scalar occurs on both sides. The first-factor shift comparison is unsigned. Thus the displayed product equalities use exactly the fixed tensor/shift maps. No extraction order or factor order changes, so no extra Koszul sign is introduced.
